title: Why your object copy changed the original
hook: I EDITED THE COPY. THE ORIGINAL CHANGED.
question: structuredClone() or JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())?
fact_source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Spread_syntax (spread effectively goes one level deep when copying) ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/structuredClone (creates a deep clone)

scenes.headline: Your copy changed the original
scenes.sub: You edited copy. user changed too.
scenes.voice: You copy an object with spread, change the copy's city, and the original user changes too?
scenes.caption: You copy an object with {...user}, change the copy's city, and the original changes too?

scenes.headline: Spread copies one level deep
scenes.voice: Spread only copies one level deep. Nested objects like address are shared, not copied.
scenes.caption: Spread only copies one level deep. Nested objects like address are shared, not copied.

scenes.headline: Use structuredClone
scenes.voice: Use structured clone. It copies every nested level, so the original stays safe.
scenes.caption: Use structuredClone(). It copies every nested level, so the original stays safe.

scenes.headline: Original stays untouched
scenes.voice: Now the original keeps Delhi. Zero shared nested objects, zero surprise bugs.
scenes.caption: Now the original keeps 'Delhi'. Zero shared nested objects, zero surprise bugs.

scenes.voice: For deep copies, which do you use: structured clone, or JSON parse of JSON stringify? Comment your answer.
scenes.caption: For deep copies, which do you use: structuredClone(), or JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())? Comment your answer.

facebook.hook: SPREAD COPY? YOUR ORIGINAL IS NOT SAFE

hook.voice: Spread looks like a full copy. But change a nested field, and the original object changes with it.
hook.caption: {...obj} looks like a full copy. But change a nested field, and the original object changes with it.
hook.headline: {...obj} is not a deep copy
